nodes.name: Callback requested
nodes.notes: Takes a token and nothing else. Any phone number in the body is ignored - see the next node.

nodes.name: Ask the portal what to dial
nodes.notes:
This is the anti-abuse design. A dialler that accepts a phone number from whoever reaches its webhook is toll fraud waiting to happen, and no shared secret fixes that as cleanly as not accepting the number. Whoever calls this webhook can only ask for a call the portal already queued, to the number the portal already chose. A forged token 404s here and the workflow stops.

The portal URL is fixed in this node rather than taken from the request, because a resolver address supplied by the caller is no protection at all.

nodes.name: Place the call
nodes.notes:
A Redirect rather than inline TwiML: the portal decides what is said, in the citizen's chosen language, at the moment the call connects - so nothing about anybody's grievance passes through this workflow.

No $env anywhere: this n8n runs with task runners enabled, which blocks $env inside expressions, and a node that reaches for one produces nothing rather than failing.

main.node: Ask the portal what to dial
